cap.proof: Let's start with your role. As CFO, what were you responsible for?
cap.mistake: No warning about whom the lawyer represents before the questions start and/or fails to explain privilege.

skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: No statement that the Company is the client, that counsel does not represent Fastow, or that counsel cannot advise him; questioning starts at T6 with no warning.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: Privilege is never mentioned, and nothing says the Company controls it or may share what he says.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T4 sets out ground rules: complete answers, flagging speculation, separating memory from reconstruction, asking for clarification. Tone is professional throughout.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asks 'Is that all right?' about ground rules only; there is no Upjohn warning to confirm and no invitation to ask questions about representation.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T372 covers confidentiality, keeping documents, not discussing with other witnesses, 'We may follow up', and 'Anything to add or correct?'. Next steps are thin.

moments.text: Interviewer introduces himself and states the topic, but gives no statement about who the lawyer represents.
Sets ground rules on speculation, recollection versus reconstruction, and asking for clarification; asks if that is all right.
Closes with confidentiality, keep documents and notes, do not discuss with other witnesses, possible follow-up, and asks for anything to add or correct.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations at T14, T30, T42 and T78 let him walk through LJM1, the unwind, Chewco and LJM2 before narrowing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moves from role and background (T6-T13) to LJM1, then Chewco, controls, and 2001 events, narrowing to specifics at each step.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear. T50 ('Was one aim of choosing Mr. Kopper to avoid that disclosure?') is leading and a little loaded.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Neutral and courteous throughout, even when confronting contradictions (T250, T304, T330). Stays in control without hostility.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Departs from the outline to follow answers: T73-74, T140-142, T250, T304-306, T330. Some areas (T264-271) are handled more by routine than adaptation.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Open invitation to describe how the Rhythms hedge was unwound, letting the witness narrate first.
Open invitation about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Challenged most evasions: the Foundation's Southampton investment (T149, T154), the Raptor utilization claim (T250), the $10M buyout (T304-306), and the payment (T330). Some answers, like T77 on Chewco's affiliation, were left unchallenged.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Covers who, what, when and how for most events, including the Southampton timing and amounts, Raptor approvals and the buyout figure. Some amounts and dates stay loose.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Asks for notes and minutes (T60), shows the Nov 5 minutes (T68), the Southampton agreement (T126) and the LJM2 report (T192), and asks for the Chewco note (T298).

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separates first-hand from secondhand knowledge: 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' (T54), 'How do you know that?' (T340), and 'did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?' (T362).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: Asks who else to talk to (T350-T353), who in Causey's group (T40), and who from legal (T320), naming Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon and counsel.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: Asks about minutes, deal files, approval sheets, the Foundation's account statements, and personal notes and emails, including where they are kept (T365-T371).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Asks how certain he is about the $4.5M (T142), the Finance Committee figure (T214, T220), the timing of the counsel call (T316), and asks for best estimates (T116-T117).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed up most key leads, but the Mordaunt investment in Southampton Place (T169) was never pursued, which caps this at 3.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
How certain are you of that figure?
Puts the 'tremendous utilization' minutes against the information that Talon had no derivatives yet, and asks the witness to reconcile them.
How do you know that?
Asks whether he saw Glisan's role himself or was told, separating personal knowledge from secondhand information.
Asks who else should be interviewed, leading to Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon and the auditors.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Each document is shown with authentication: who prepared it, whether he recognizes it, and whether it is a complete copy (T68-T70, T126-T131, T192-T197, T254-T257). The Chewco note is introduced with a non-accusatory framing.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Asks for his memory first: the Nov 5 call (T59-T67) before the minutes, Southampton (T124) before the agreement, and Talon's derivatives (T246) before the minutes.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Descriptions match the record: the 193/278/2,500% returns, the 'not at risk' quote, the $4.5M on $25,000, the 17.95% versus 51% figures, and the $1M versus $10.5M figures.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Uses neutral framing such as 'Help me understand how those fit together' (T148, T250, T304) and 'Help me understand the difference' (T240) without concluding the witness was lying.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: Gives him room to explain each inconsistency (T148-T149, T240-T241, T260-T263, T304-T305) and confirms his account before moving on (T330-T331).

moments.text: Asks what else was happening around the time of the Nov 5 call before showing the minutes, to refresh memory first.
Shows the Nov 5, 1997 Executive Committee minutes and asks whether he recognizes them, then asks who prepared them (T70).
Asks about Southampton Place first (T124), then shows the March 20, 2000 partnership agreement and asks whether he recognizes it.
Shows the October 2000 LJM2 investor report, asks whether he recognizes it, who prepared it, and whether it is complete.
I'm not suggesting you wrote it.

big_mistakes.proof: Let's start with your role. As CFO, what were you responsible for?
big_mistakes.mistake: No warning about whom the lawyer represents before the questions start and/or fails to explain privilege.

missed_opportunities: T169: Kristina Mordaunt, a named Enron investor in Southampton Place, was never asked about her investment, its amount, or her payout. Ask: “What did Kristina Mordaunt invest in Southampton Place, when, who invited her, and what did she receive back?”

T77: He said Chewco was not affiliated with Enron and Kopper was investing on his own account, and this was not tested against his earlier account of Skilling's approval. Ask: “If Chewco was Michael's own investment, who else at Enron was told it was his, and when did you first tell them?”
